### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `22a2893f0c4a6a38bc22fefbf6f94b681c76ced2` — the merge of head `586d7b57ff2df2e9427e18860e2961abab2bba12` into base `2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 22a2893f0c4a6a38bc22fefbf6f94b681c76ced2 && git checkout 22a2893f0c4a6a38bc22fefbf6f94b681c76ced2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d 586d7b57ff2df2e9427e18860e2961abab2bba12 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d && git merge --no-ff 586d7b57ff2df2e9427e18860e2961abab2bba12

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `693b450c908e9cfb78e2f5618705c4c522effde6`
Local-runs: none

PR #23301 for card #22861 (ADR-0139 E2), judged on the net diff against `main` (merge-base 175e8d4149; 13 files, +1106 / -116), the card's 17 comments (ruling 6121741984, letter A with both sub-questions; seat answer 6123453723; the #23009 pointers 6137591851 and 6139288051; claim 6145796666; delivery report 6150445600) and the check-runs on this head. Read-only: nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on this head, as read:** 33 of 38 completed, every completed one `success` or an expected `skipped`. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Check Changeset` and `Test Core (5/6)` are `success`. Still `in_progress` at this read, so not judged here: `Test Core (1/6)`, `(2/6)`, `(3/6)`, `(4/6)`, `(6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace`. The queue's own all-green condition waits on those whatever this record says.

### ① Derived judgments

The request-level accept set (REST, a JSON `where`) is unchanged by construction: no brand survives JSON, the comparand door's `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 for a plain object in a list slot is byte-identical, and `parseFilterAST` still refuses the array sugar's `in` leaf 400 (pinned). Every change below is on the in-process engine API of `@objectstack/objectql`, and one on `@objectstack/core`.

Accept set, each judged against ADR-0139 D1 / D2 / D5 as amended by ruling 6121741984 (A):

1. Read verbs (`find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`), a caller-written `$in` leaf in `where`: `main` refused it `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 (the interim `refuseUncomposedReadableIds`); the head composes it immediately before the driver call into `ReadableIds.compose(leaf, scope)` or `$in: []`. **Right** — D2 as amended; the ruling orders the interim refusal to move to the boundary as the refusal of what cannot be composed, and the claim cites the negating text.
2. Read verbs, a leaf written by an object-scoped middleware or a `beforeFind` hook: `main` handed it to the driver uncomposed (measured in 6119740461, P2 and P3); the head composes it on all four verbs (pinned). **Right** — the ruling's pin list.
3. Read verbs, a leaf at any position but a `$in` comparand (equality, `$nin`, a list member, a `$between` endpoint; caller- or chain-written): refused 500 by name at the door and again at the boundary. **Right** — D1's last paragraph.
4. `update` / `delete`: the caller's leaf stays refused at the door; a chain-written one, which on `main` reached `updateMany` (P5c), is refused 500 at the executor's entry, ahead of the prior-row reads. **Right** — D1; the position per 6123453723 finding 3.
5. `having` and an aggregation's own `filter`: refused at the door as before, and at the boundary for a chain-written one. **Right** — D1 names `having`; the having door, previously pinned by nothing (card body), is now pinned.
6. A composed leaf the engine did not build: chain-written, 500 (new: `main`'s interim asked `isReadableIds`, which answers false for a composed leaf, so it passed); caller-written, the door's 400 (unchanged). **Right** — the spec's own text on `ComposedReadableIds`: never trusted as a scope someone else already resolved.
7. D5's three classes (a delegated caller via `onBehalfOf.userId`; a parent `hasObjectMiddleware` narrows; a parent whose `resolveDatasourceBinding` differs from the read object's): 500 by name, before any security call (pinned, including that neither half is asked). **Right** — D5, no silent fallback.
8. The `where` array form: a leaf the lowering puts into a non-`$in` position is refused 500 by name (on `main` the interim ran on the object branch only). **Right** — the card body's carried item and the ruling's pin.
9. Composition answers `$in: []` for: `canReadObject` false or a throw; a service without `canReadObject` whose `explain({ object, operation: 'read' }).allowed` is not `true`; an absent, nothing-answering, throwing or half-capable service (one `warn` per engine per state, no verdict cached); `getReadFilter` throwing or answering a non-filter; `RLS_DENY_FILTER` by identity; a parent the registry does not hold. **Right** — D2 steps 1 and 2; the `explain` fallback is the contract's own prescription ("the fallback for an absent method is NOT admit"), and `ExplainAccessRequest` takes exactly `{ object, operation }`.
10. The scope is `getReadFilter`'s answer by reference, marked `'policy'` through `markFilterSubtreeProvenance`, not re-lowered; the tenant wall is not composed. **Right** — D2 step 3; the lowering parenthetical was read by the seat (6123453723 finding 2) as what P's own direct read does with its policy scope, which is nothing, and the record text was left at the ruled sentence. Not a fork.
11. Nothing memoised; one `canReadObject` and one `getReadFilter` per distinct parent per read (pinned on two leaves over one parent beside one over another). **Right** — D2.
12. Fork clause: the AST is final at each driver call. `find` and `findOne` compose after `triggerHooks('beforeFind')` and `buildDriverOptions`; `count` composes before `driver.count`, and its no-`count` fallback goes through `find`'s own boundary; `aggregate` composes once and both exclusive paths consume it (`drv.aggregate(object, ast, …)`, and the rows path's `{ ...ast }` with the `having` and aggregation keys deleted and `where` by reference), with the boundary re-checking `having` and `aggregations[i].filter` after the chain. Read on this head. **Right** — not tripped. A leaf inside a nested-relation condition meets the boundary of the sub-read that `lowerRelationConditions` issues through `this.find(site.target, …)`, so no path to a driver bypasses the seam.
13. `@objectstack/core` `resolveFilterTokens`: a branded leaf beside a resolved placeholder is returned by reference (on `main` it was rebuilt as an unbranded `{ object }`), and `hasFilterToken` treats the leaf as a comparand. **Right** — ruling sub-question 1; pinned in core and, through core's `dist/`, at the engine.
14. The three #23009 notes (a deny ANDed with another layer, a cross-format copy of the sentinel, sharing's `{ id: '__deny_all__' }`): composed as ordinary scopes, each pinned to match no parent row beside a lit control; no fast path added. **Right** — D2 step 2 is by identity, and the spec seat kept `getReadFilter`'s shape as it is.

Public surface:

15. `@objectstack/objectql`: `ObjectQL.registerSecurityServiceSource(source)`, taking a thunk that returns `unknown` and returning `void`, is a **new public member of a class that both `exports` entries publish** (`.` to `dist/index.d.ts` and `./core` to `dist/core.d.ts`; each carries `export { ObjectQL, ObjectRepository, ScopedContext } from './engine.js'`). The content is right (granted in 6123453723 Q2; read at use, never at init; unregistered is a defined fail-closed state; last registration wins). Its **declaration is wrong**: a new public member on a published class expands the public surface. See ②.
16. The new exports of `filter-comparand-shape.ts` (`collectComposableReadableIds`, `composeReadableIdsLeaves`, `readableIdsRefusalError`, `describeReadableIdsLeaf`, `ComposableReadableIdsSite`) are re-exported by neither `index.ts` nor `core.ts`: shipped bytes, not published surface. **Right** — nothing owed.
17. `IObjectQLEngine` unchanged; `packages/spec/**` untouched, so the path limb is not hit; `ObjectQLPlugin`'s signature unchanged (its `init` now calls the new method on a `ql` typed `ObjectQL`); no new error code (`INTERNAL_ERROR` is a ledger code); the ADR anchor invariant rewritten to the new rule (`check:adr-anchors` runs inside `Lint & Repo Gates`, `success`). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/objectql: minor` — matches the diff: a new public member on `ObjectQL` and new behaviour; no entry-reachable name removed or renamed (`refuseUncomposedReadableIds` was module-private). **Right.**
- `@objectstack/core: patch` — a behaviour fix in `resolveFilterTokens`, no signature change. **Right.**
- Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed and none is written; the changeset body carries the migration-free before/after; `Check Changeset` is `success`. **Right.**
- **`Clause-②: no` is wrong on the public-surface limb.** The accept-set limb is correctly `no`: the interim 500 is a refusal the accepted D2 text negates ("every `ReadableIds` leaf is replaced by its composed form, still branded, before any driver sees it"), the claim cites that text, and every other refusal is kept or narrowed under D1 / D5. The public-surface limb is not `no`: `registerSecurityServiceSource` is reachable from both `exports` entries of a published package, which is 扩大公开面 under the claim rule's definition (「公开面 = 包构建后的入口声明所达,⛔ 不只数入口的再导出清单」) and the spec lane's criterion (「放宽接受集或扩大公开面的卡,不论多小,即条款②」). The seat's grant (6123453723 Q2) judged the member against `IObjectQLEngine` membership, a narrower test than the rule's; the landing rule reads 「错误的 `no` 是可审计的假申报」. The declaration sits on three carriers: the claim (6145796666), the PR body's line 2, and the changeset body. Remedy, either arm: (i) flip the line to `yes` on all three — the `minor` already satisfies "`yes` takes at least `minor`"; or (ii) take the seam off the published surface and keep `no`: a symbol-keyed engine slot, as `plugin.ts` already does with `SKIP_SCHEMA_SYNC_ENGINE_KEY`, or a module export of `engine.ts` that `index.ts` and `core.ts` do not re-export. A fresh record is owed on the resulting head either way.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none in the delivery report (6150445600). Flags from the PR's acceptance notes and the report's deviations, each answered:

1. **Unregistered parent answered `$in: []`, unasked.** Accepted. D4 orders exclusion for a row naming an unregistered object, the leaf is in none of D5's classes, and the answer is fail-closed. Noted, not required: it is the one deny arm that logs nothing, where the absent-service and throw arms `warn`.
2. **One new public method, not an `IObjectQLEngine` member.** It is a public-surface addition of `@objectstack/objectql` — the ② finding. Escalated to the seat as the one defect of this head.
3. **D5.2 over-inclusion** (plugin-security's own object-scoped doors count as middleware-gated). Accepted. D5.2's text errs to the bound, and the ruling's evidence (6121741984, from 6119740461's D5 readings) already read that over-inclusion as the bound's cost.
4. **No live exposure.** Accepted. Zero non-test producers (card body; 6137591851), no driver evaluates the composed leaf before E3 / E4, and the driver-side refusal of an uncomposed leaf is E3 / E4's by D2's last paragraph.
5. **`resolveFilterTokens` exempts only `Date` among class instances** (carrier none, a read-only inference). Accepted as a note. Not reproduced, so no card is owed under Prime Directive #10, and this diff does not touch that branch.
6. **File surface beyond the claim** (`filter-comparand-shape.ts`, the ADR anchor JSON, three engine test doubles). Accepted. `filter-comparand-shape.ts` is in the original claim's surface (6119321139), which the ruling re-used; the anchor file is `check:adr-anchors`'s own requirement once the invariant it quoted was removed, and `scripts/adr-anchors/` is not a governed surface; the doubles follow `ObjectQLPlugin.init`'s new call.
7. **`main` moved three commits after this head, not re-merged.** Accepted. CI runs on the merge ref, and the head's check-runs are the verdict.
8. **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally.** Accepted. It rides `Lint & Repo Gates`, `success` on this head.
9. **Fork clause.** Not tripped, confirmed by this read (① item 12).
10. **The #23009 notes** (composite deny, dual-package identity, sharing's deny-all). Accepted as fail-safe populations pinned beside a lit control (① item 14).

Governed surfaces: none touched (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/workflows/**` are all absent from the file list); `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`. Size +1106 / -116, under the 3,000-line threshold. Head repo equals base repo, so not a fork proposal.

One defect on this head: the `Clause-②: no` declaration on a diff that adds a public member to a published class (② above). Everything else judged here is right. What is owed is a patch round that corrects the declaration, or takes the member off the published surface, and a fresh record on the new head.

Reviewed-by: `session_01P88ehrZ6hM19hBzdpsQTTo`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
